_comment: The SCA twin of unverified-vendor-source: the same unfetchable VENDOR declaration over the same minified file, carried in the source archive. Nothing about the diagnosis changes - an unfetchable declaration buys no exemption, and a minified file cannot be reviewed - but the archive is where the readable build has to land, so this pins the SCA branch of untrusted-minified-library and the source-code-submission link that goes with it. The XPI here also ships a VENDORS.md of its own, which in a source-code submission belongs in the archive - the copy the reviewer reads and the build installs from - so sca-xpi-declares-vendoring reports it, naming the file(s) on the finding. It narrows nothing here - the archive is still reviewed in full.
